verdict.rationale: Mailchimp does ship a genuinely separate transactional product (Mandrill) with its own API/SMTP, dedicated IPs, and allow/deny suppression lists distinct from the Marketing API's audience/unsubscribe system (mailchimp-docs-2, -6, -7, -17, -18), which supports the story's premise of separate templates/suppression/reputation. However, a hands-on community report describes Mailchimp silently shutting off Mandrill (transactional) sending because of a single complaint tied to marketing-style use, and another notes the two systems still aren't well integrated years after merging — concrete evidence that the reputation/operational separation is not as clean in practice as documented. missing for 10: first-party documentation explicitly confirming transactional sends bypass marketing unsubscribe/suppression lists, and independent proof that a marketing unsubscribe never blocks a transactional receipt.
